blocks.x: Downtown Winnipeg has plenty of empty office space, and City housing programs aim to add homes there. [CBRE reports](https://mktgdocs.cbre.com/2299/635166d3-3766-4bba-836b-1640e9e191dc-610961676/Winnipeg_Office_Figures_Q3_202.pdf) downtown office vacancy of 17.3% in Q3 2026, and many older buildings still sit partly empty. An office to residential conversion in Winnipeg can work, but only in the right building.

Converting empty offices into apartments sounds like an obvious fix, and the City's Housing Accelerator Fund work included a [Vacant Building Grant](https://www.winnipeg.ca/building-development/housing/housing-accelerator-fund/vacant-building-grant) that accepted conversions to housing from office use (intake closed August 17, 2026).

But [CBRE's Winnipeg managing director said in January 2026](https://www.cbre.com/insights/articles/whats-ahead-for-winnipeg-commercial-real-estate-in-2026) that the city isn't seeing many office conversions. Not every office building makes a good apartment building.
Which Winnipeg office buildings convert well to residential
**Good candidates usually have:**
**Shallow floor plates.** Bedrooms generally need windows, so narrow buildings are far easier to lay out.
**Lots of windows,** ideally operable or replaceable.
**Older Class B or C office space** that struggles to compete with newer towers for office tenants.
**Good locations** near transit, groceries, the Exchange District or amenities residents want.
**Reasonable structure and floor-to-floor heights** to fit new plumbing and ventilation.
**Harder candidates:** deep floor plates with dark interiors, few windows, tight ceiling heights, or major structural or envelope problems.
What the renovation involves
Office-to-residential conversions are among the most complex renovations because nearly every system changes:

head: System
What changes
rows: New stacks and lines to every kitchen and bathroom
Individual suite ventilation and comfort control
Suite fire separations, sprinklers, alarms and exits for residential use
Accessible suites and common areas as required by code
Windows, insulation and air sealing for residential comfort in Winnipeg winters
Demolition, new suite walls, kitchens, bathrooms, finishes

blocks.x: Permits and approvals

Changing a building from office to residential is a change of use. It starts with a City of Winnipeg building permit application, then an [occupancy permit](/blog/occupancy-permit-change-of-use-winnipeg), and the affected parts must meet current code for residential use, including fire safety.
The City's form asks for drawings sealed by an architect or engineer when a [change in major occupancy classification](https://www.winnipeg.ca/media/6330) happens in a Part 3 building.

Zoning must allow residential use on the site. Engage an architect and code consultant early, before you commit to a purchase price. In an older building, have suspect materials [tested for asbestos](/blog/asbestos-testing-before-renovating-manitoba) before demolition starts.
Funding and incentives

Governments at all levels have introduced housing programs in recent years, including federal [Housing Accelerator Fund](https://www.winnipeg.ca/building-development/housing/housing-accelerator-fund) money tied to Winnipeg zoning changes. That work included the Vacant Building Grant, now closed, and a Heritage Conversion Program led by CentreVenture for downtown heritage residential conversions. Ask CentreVenture whether that program is still open.

The City's [Heritage & Economic Development Incentive](https://www.winnipeg.ca/building-development/housing/heritage-economic-development-incentive) lists new downtown residential projects of at least five units among its eligible projects, though its page doesn't say whether it is taking applications. Programs and eligibility change often, so check current City of Winnipeg, Province of Manitoba and federal (CMHC) programs before budgeting. This is general information, not legal or financial advice.
Five steps to evaluate a conversion
**Feasibility study:** floor plates, windows, structure, code path.
**Test fit:** how many suites, what sizes, what rents.
**Cost estimate** from a contractor who has walked the building and read the drawings.
**Financing and incentives** review.
**Go or no-go** before acquiring or committing capital.
The bottom line
Conversions can turn an empty office into much-needed housing, but only in the right building. Start with feasibility and real costs, not assumptions.
